issue: Can a federal prisoner use the § 2255(e) escape hatch to bring a § 2241 petition challenging a sentence, such as a career-offender designation, without showing actual innocence of the underlying crime of conviction?

sides.position: Escape hatch jurisdiction is available for sentencing challenges that do not require the petitioner to show actual innocence of the offense of conviction.
cases: United States v. Wheeler, 886 F.3d 415 (4th Cir. 2018)

sides.position: Escape hatch jurisdiction requires a showing of actual innocence of the crime of conviction, and a legal challenge to Guidelines classification, such as career-offender status, does not qualify.

this_court: The majority apparently allowed the career-offender sentencing challenge through the escape hatch, which the dissent says departs from Ninth Circuit precedent requiring actual innocence of the crime of conviction.
quote: Second, I recognize that there is currently a circuit split on this issue. Some other circuits have allowed sentencing challenges similar to Allen's under the escape hatch.
cite: Michael Allen v. Richard Ives, No. 18-35001 (9th Cir. 2020)
